reader.identity: rr-euf1 cold reader (Type 2 TASK, dispatched by a HELP_HUMAN session)
reader.separation: Took no part in producing the files. Read only the files in rr-euf1/in; opened no repository, git history, session, conversation or web page; used no network.

Q-1.statement: The package reserves the replacement decision to the owner (citing PRD §8 V4-REP-01 and EXAMINATION §7). Its identity is pkg:app-v4:replacement:FX-RP1 and it requests act kind A16, a code no supplied file defines.

fields.subject_revision: ILLUSTRATIVE (SQ example; not a real candidate)

Q-2.statement: The candidate revision is a placeholder copied from the SQ example, not a real candidate. The local-host CIR does not supply an App candidate because no candidate is identified and host joins are deferred, so the packet does not establish one candidate across both obligations.

Q-3.statement: Six elements are marked met on illustrative step results. Restart is not_met because step S11-6 was recorded blocked, so the obligation is not_met. It is not established because the obligation is not met and none of the 15 step results resolves to records of an identified candidate. The six V4-EXM-12 steps are set outside the core loop.

Q-4.statement: The joined-journey obligation is incomplete. P20-A is not counted as a completed witness, no acceptance act is cited, there is no independent review record, and its result ref names an example case that was not run.

Q-5.statement: The replacement evidence is not complete: the core loop is not established, the journey is not established, and the candidate is not reconciled.

Q-6.statement: There are six gaps. Four bear on the replacement conditions, and two (continuity, adoption) are carried for the owner but are not replacement conditions. The named supplier deliverables are DEL-09-02, DEL-09-07, DEL-11-01 and DEL-11-02, with the SWBPIPE owner and affected project owners also named. Practitioner validation is not listed as a gap.

Q-7.statement: Only ALT-PUBLISHED ends v3.0.1's role as the published fallback, and it is also a public-release act that the owner decides separately. None of the four alternatives retires anything.

Q-8.statement: The disposition record says not_presented, because this is an EU-F1 fixture prepared only for the consumption check. It records no owner act and states that none is implied. v3.0.1 remains the fallback.

Q-9.statement: Practitioner validation is not agreed: no period or activities are agreed and no practitioner use has occurred. Both the packet and the first-cut input say it is not a replacement condition.

Q-10.statement: Whatever its evidence, the packet never establishes six things: a replacement decision, public release, retirement, professional reliance, consumer adoption, or practitioner validation.

Q-11.statement: The continuity input reports that the thesis tree identity matches at a named commit. It notes limits: working bytes were not compared and attribution was not inspected. The fallback's identity was not re-checked against the remote release, the archive check was not run, and neither the continuing-obligation dispositions nor the consumer adoption status is supplied.

Q-12.statement: The packet's evidence standing is illustrative. It is built from schema examples and first-cut interfaces, and by the legend's definition nothing in it can establish an obligation.

issues.statement: The package requests actKind "A16", but no supplied file says what A16 means. A decision maker cannot tell from these files what kind of act is being asked for.

issues.about: Element statuses read as favourable on unresolved, illustrative steps
issues.statement: Six core-loop elements show status "met", yet the packet lists all 15 counted steps (including every step behind those six) as unresolved_steps, and every result record is marked ILLUSTRATIVE. Only established=false and the G-CL-EVIDENCE gap show that "met" carries no evidential weight. A hurried reader could take "met" as proven.

The package asks whether the candidate "replaces the v3.0.1 fallback", but under ALT-OWN-USE v3.0.1 stays published and remains the fallback. The files do not say what that alternative replaces in terms of the stated subject, beyond the owner moving their own work.

The packet's journey.receipts says total 0 and unresolvable 0, matching the dossier's handoff_del_11_03 (empty receipts). The same dossier's handoff_del_09_11 lists one receipt, RC-1, that was unresolvable when written. The packet does not explain why that receipt is not counted.

The SQ dossier names an independent examiner and a review record (EXP-RX-02, illustrative) for the standalone scenarios, while the packet reports independent_review "absent" for the journey, and the CIR says the journey's examiner is not yet named. These concern different obligations, but no file makes that explicit.

Several terms are never defined in the supplied files: "P20-A" (I infer, but cannot confirm, that it means case LHQ-20 via p20a_result_ref); "O-C" and "RQ-LHQ-1" in G-CAND-JOINED; "O-F" as the recorder; and the DECISION-3, DEP-001, OI-0xx, R23-32 and B-HTML references.

The basis quotations and the reserved-by statements cite docs/PRD.md, docs/EXAMINATION.md, the DEL-11-03 ScopeOfWork, REFERENCES.md, BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md and ARCHIVES.md by reference and hash. None is in the input set, so a reader cannot check the quotes or the ALT-PUBLISHED inference about v3.0.x update offers.

issues.about: Weak v3.0.1 comparison basis and unchecked fallback identity
issues.statement: The first condition asks for the core loop "at least at v3.0.1's level". Yet the baseline says its v3 references come from a v3.0.0-era development candidate that is not an ancestor of the v3.0.1 source, and that the fallback identity was not re-checked against the remote release. No file says how "v3.0.1's level" is to be judged.

issues.about: Continuity and practitioner inputs sourced from a schema
issues.statement: Items S-4 and S-5 are 'first_cut_interface' records whose source is the packet-manifest schema's $defs, not a record from the owning deliverables (DEL-11-01, DEL-09-12). So the 'thesis_identity: matches' result rests on a first-cut input. Its git method cannot be checked from the supplied files.

issues.about: Points of need in a never-presented fixture
issues.statement: Every gap's point of need is 'before the package is presented', while the package's purpose says it is not for presentation to the owner and the disposition says no owner act is requested. This is consistent for a fixture, but a reader could be unsure whether these gaps block anything.

issues.about: Placeholder hashes in the LHQ dossier
issues.statement: The LHQ dossier's record_set uses placeholder sha256 values (all 1s and all 2s) and invented paths. They are marked invented, but they show the journey evidence carries no real records.
